_meta.description: Machine-readable component library for the robotics reference pack. Single source of truth for specs and datasheet URLs. Specs were checked against manufacturer/distributor pages on 2026-11-14; 'verified_url': false means the link follows the vendor's standard pattern but was not confirmed.
_meta.units: SI unless noted; voltages in V, currents in A, dimensions in mm

schema.id: stable key used by project docs
schema.used_in: project ids: swerve3, ftc_decode, arm4dof, diffdrive, tripod
schema.key_specs: datasheet-derived numbers an agent needs for power, wiring and software
schema.gotchas: integration traps found while compiling this pack

components.name: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B

key_specs.power_input: 5 V via USB-C or GPIO header, 3 A minimum (2.5 A ok if USB peripherals < 500 mA)

gotchas: Powering via GPIO 5 V pins bypasses the USB-C input protection; use a regulated, low-ripple 5.1 V supply that can hold 3 A.
Linux is not real-time: step-pulse generation or tight PID loops on the Pi will jitter. Offload to an MCU or use DMA-timed waveforms (pigpio) or driver-side motion (TMC2209 VACTUAL).
Under-voltage (lightning bolt / throttled flag) causes CPU throttling and SD-card corruption; check `vcgencmd get_throttled` during bring-up.

components.name: Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040)

key_specs.gpio: 26 user GPIO (GP0-GP22, GP26-GP28), 3 of which are ADC
key_specs.pio: 2 PIO blocks x 4 state machines (use for quadrature decode and pulse-width capture)
key_specs.power_input: VSYS 1.8-5.5 V (on-board buck-boost to 3.3 V); VBUS 5 V from USB

gotchas: Any sensor output that swings to 5 V (e.g., Pololu 37D Hall encoder powered at 5 V) must be level-shifted or divided before reaching a GPIO.
Use PIO quadrature decoding (pico-examples/pio/quadrature_encoder) instead of GPIO interrupts for >1 encoder at high count rates.

components.name: ESP32 (e.g., ESP32-WROOM-32E dev board)

key_specs.cpu: Xtensa dual-core LX6 up to 240 MHz
key_specs.pwm: LED PWM (LEDC) up to 16 channels + MCPWM (motor PWM) peripheral
key_specs.strapping_pins: GPIO0, 2, 5, 12 (MTDI), 15 (MTDO) - avoid for outputs that are pulled at boot

interfaces: SPI (VSPI: 18 SCK, 19 MISO, 23 MOSI, 5 CS by convention)
gotchas: GPIO12 high at boot selects 1.8 V flash on many modules -> boot failure; never pull it up.
ADC2 pins are unusable while Wi-Fi is active.
Wi-Fi TX bursts draw ~250-350 mA peaks; give the 3.3 V rail bulk capacitance and do not share it with servos.

components.name: Arduino UNO R3 (A000066)

key_specs.mcu: ATmega328P @16 MHz, 2 kB SRAM, 32 kB flash, 1 kB EEPROM
key_specs.vin_recommended: 7-12 V (limits 6-20 V); above 12 V the linear regulator may overheat
key_specs.io: 14 digital (6 PWM: D3, D5, D6, D9, D10, D11), 6 analog
key_specs.external_interrupts: Only D2 (INT0) and D3 (INT1); others need pin-change interrupts

interfaces: SPI (D10 SS, D11 MOSI, D12 MISO, D13 SCK)
gotchas: Servo library uses Timer1 and disables analogWrite() on D9 and D10.
The on-board 5 V linear regulator dissipates (Vin - 5) x I; at 12 V in, a few hundred mA of servo current will overheat it. Power servos from a separate 5-6 V buck.
Only two hardware interrupt pins: plan encoder wiring before assigning pins.

components.name: REV Control Hub (REV-31-1595)

key_specs.motor_ports: 4 (JST VH 2-pin) with 4 quadrature encoder ports (JST PH 4-pin)
key_specs.servo_ports: 6 (0.1 in header), 500-2500 us extended range; ports share power in pairs (0-1, 2-3, 4-5)
key_specs.servo_plus_5v_budget: 5 A total shared across all servo ports and +5 V aux ports
key_specs.i2c: 4 independent buses, 3.3 V, 100/400 kHz, 500 mA total supply
key_specs.battery: 12 V NiMH FTC battery via XT30; second XT30 port daisy-chains an Expansion Hub
key_specs.hw_encoder_ports: Encoder ports 0 and 3 are hardware-decoded (best for high-speed motors such as flywheels)

gotchas: Internal IMU lives on I2C bus 0; put add-on I2C devices on buses 1-3.
High-current servos: use ports 0, 2, 4 (one per power pair) or add a Servo Power Module.
Absolute (pulse) outputs of encoders like the REV Through Bore are not supported on hub encoder ports - quadrature only.

datasheets.label: Control system overview / Control Hub specs

components.name: REV Expansion Hub (REV-31-1153)

key_specs.aux_5v: 2 ports, 5 V / 2 A (shares 5 A budget with servos)
key_specs.size_mm: 143 x 103 x 29.5, mounting holes on 16 mm spacing

gotchas: Address the hub as 'Expansion Hub 2' in the robot configuration; bulk-read both hubs each loop.

components.name: goBILDA Pinpoint Odometry Computer (3110-0002-0001; V2 is 3110-0002-0002)

key_specs.function: Fuses 2 dead-wheel quadrature encoders with an internal IMU

gotchas: Robot must be stationary during resetPosAndIMU()/recalibrateIMU() (~0.25 s).
Set encoder resolution (goBILDA_4_BAR_POD) and X/Y pod offsets in mm relative to the tracking point; sign convention: left of center is positive for X pod offset.

components.name: goBILDA 4-Bar Odometry Pod, 32 mm wheel (3110-0001-0002)

key_specs.mounting: fits inside 43 x 43 mm profiles (e.g., goBILDA 1120 U-channel), M4 hardware

gotchas: Spring preload is factory-tuned; do not add extra downforce.

components.name: goBILDA 5203 Series Yellow Jacket planetary gear motor

key_specs.encoder: Hall quadrature, 3.3-5 V, 28 counts per motor revolution x gear ratio at output
key_specs.mounting: 4x M4 x 10 mm deep on 16 mm square goBILDA pattern

gotchas: Flywheels: choose 1:1 or 3.7:1 and put their encoders on hardware-decoded ports 0/3.

datasheets.label: Example product page with full specs (99.5:1)

components.name: REV Color Sensor V3 (REV-31-1557) - assumed model
gotchas: Fixed address: one sensor per I2C bus (or add an I2C mux). Shares 0x52 with the REV 2m Distance Sensor.
Color values differ between V2 and V3; recalibrate thresholds per sensor under match lighting.

components.name: ST ISM330DHCX 6-axis IMU

key_specs.extras: FIFO, machine-learning core, finite state machine, sensor hub
key_specs.package: LGA-14L 2.5 x 3.0 x 0.83 mm (use a breakout, e.g., Adafruit/SparkFun)

gotchas: Mount near the chassis center of rotation, rigidly, away from motor magnets; vibration-isolate if wheels are hard.
Run gyro bias calibration at startup while stationary; integrate gyro Z for heading and fuse with wheel odometry.

components.name: Sharp GP2Y0E03 IR distance sensor

key_specs.pins: VDD, Vout(A), GND, VIN(IO), GPIO1, SCL, SDA

gotchas: All units share one address -> use a TCA9548A mux (as built) or E-Fuse reprogramming (permanent, risky).
VIN(IO) sets the I2C logic level; tie to 3.3 V on a 3.3 V bus.
GPIO1 controls active/standby; tie high (to VIN(IO)) for always-on.
IR sensors struggle on black/very shiny surfaces and in sunlight.

components.name: TI TCA9548A 8-channel I2C switch/mux

key_specs.control: single 8-bit register, one bit per channel; any combination may be enabled
key_specs.reset: active-low RESET to recover a stuck downstream bus
key_specs.voltage_translation: yes - pass gates limited by VCC

gotchas: Downstream channels need their own pull-ups if the breakout lacks them.
Select exactly one channel when talking to identical-address devices.

components.name: REV Through Bore Encoder V2

key_specs.absolute_pulse_v1_reference: period 1025 us (975.6 Hz), 1 us = 0 deg, 1024 us = 360 deg, 10-bit
key_specs.bore: 1/2 in hex default; inserts for 3/8 in hex, 5 mm hex, 1/4 in round
key_specs.zero: factory-calibrated to case notch (do not disassemble)

gotchas: SKU naming is inconsistent across REV pages (REV-11-1271 vs REV-11-3174); confirm which unit you have and read its spec page for supply/logic levels.
Power from 3.3 V when connecting directly to a 3.3 V MCU unless the spec page confirms 3.3 V logic at 5 V supply.
Read the absolute channel with PIO/timer capture; it updates ~1 kHz, adequate for a steering loop.

components.name: ams OSRAM AS5047P 14-bit magnetic rotary encoder

key_specs.incremental: ABI up to 12-bit decimal/binary (programmable; e.g., 4000 steps = 1000 pulses/rev)
key_specs.supply: 5 V mode: VDD 4.5-5.5 V (internal LDO, 1 uF on VDD3V3); 3.3 V mode: VDD and VDD3V3 tied, 3.0-3.6 V
key_specs.spi: mode 1 (CPOL=0, CPHA=1), 16-bit frames with even parity; angle register 0x3FFF

gotchas: Needs a diametrically magnetized magnet (typ. 6 mm x 2.5 mm) centered on the axis; air gap ~0.5-3 mm per datasheet. Design a magnet pocket in CAD concentric with the shaft.
Logic levels follow VDD: at 5 V supply outputs are 5 V (fine for UNO, not for ESP32).

components.name: Pololu 37D metal gearmotor, 12 V, 64 CPR encoder (helical pinion)

key_specs.example_ratios: 10:1 1000 RPM 4.9 kg-cm; 30:1 330 RPM 14 kg-cm; 131:1, 150:1 for steering
key_specs.encoder: 64 counts per motor-shaft revolution (both edges of A and B); output CPR = 64 x gear ratio
key_specs.encoder_supply: 3.5-20 V, 10 mA max; A/B outputs swing 0 V to Vcc
key_specs.wires: red/black motor, green GND, blue Vcc, yellow A, white B
key_specs.body: 37 mm diameter; do not screw >3 mm into gearbox face holes

gotchas: Encoder minimum Vcc is 3.5 V and outputs swing to Vcc: on a 3.3 V MCU either power at 5 V and divide/level-shift A/B, or accept out-of-spec 3.3 V operation.
Do not stall at rated voltage for extended periods (Pololu FAQ: no).
Budget stall current, not running current, for fuses, wiring and driver selection.

components.name: Cytron MDD10A dual-channel 10 A motor driver

key_specs.current: 10 A continuous per channel, 30 A peak (<10 s)
key_specs.control: PWM + DIR per channel (sign-magnitude) or locked-antiphase

gotchas: No reverse-polarity protection: key the battery connector.
Use 18-20 kHz PWM to stay above audible range.

components.name: BTS7960 43 A H-bridge module (IBT-2 style, 2x Infineon BTS7960B)
components.manufacturer: Infineon (IC, now obsolete); modules are generic

key_specs.path_resistance: ~16 mOhm typ (7 mOhm high side + 9 mOhm low side)
key_specs.module_pins: RPWM, LPWM, R_EN, L_EN, R_IS, L_IS, VCC (5 V logic), GND

gotchas: IC is obsolete; successor family is BTN8982 / BTN9970. Module quality varies.
Never drive RPWM and LPWM high together.

components.name: Trinamic/ADI TMC2209 stepper driver (StepStick-style module)

key_specs.current: 2 A RMS / 2.8 A peak per coil (IC rating; modules realistically ~1.2-1.4 A RMS without active cooling)
key_specs.microstepping: 8/16/32/64 by pins; up to 256 native via UART; MicroPlyer interpolation to 256
key_specs.uart: single-wire UART on PDN_UART; 4 addresses via MS1/MS2 to share one bus
key_specs.internal_pulse_generator: VACTUAL register runs the motor at a set velocity without STEP pulses

gotchas: Set current (VREF or IRUN via UART) below the motor's rated phase current and heatsink the module.
Never disconnect a motor while the driver is powered.
Pi UART TX connects to PDN_UART through a 1 kOhm resistor; RX ties directly (single-wire half duplex).

components.name: NEMA 17 bipolar stepper (17HS4401-class reference)
components.manufacturer: various (exact model not specified by user)

key_specs.mounting: 4x M3 on 31 mm square, 22 mm pilot boss, 5 mm shaft

gotchas: Torque falls with speed; size with the pull-out torque curve, not holding torque.
Wire colors vary by vendor: identify coil pairs with a multimeter (~1.5 Ohm across a pair).

components.name: 25 kg-cm digital servo (DS3225-class reference)
components.manufacturer: various (exact model not specified by user)
gotchas: Never power from an MCU 5 V pin. Budget stall x count x 0.5 minimum, with headroom for transients; add 1000+ uF bulk capacitance at the servo bus.
Check whether yours is 180 or 270 deg before computing pulse-to-angle mapping.

components.name: LM2596 adjustable buck converter module

key_specs.efficiency: ~80% at 12 V in, 5 V / 3 A out (LM2596-5.0 typical)
key_specs.dropout_note: fixed 5 V version needs Vin >= 7 V for regulation spec

gotchas: Generic modules frequently carry counterfeit ICs and small inductors; derate to ~2 A continuous without a heatsink.
A Pi 4B wants 3 A: an LM2596 module is at its limit. Prefer a 5 A buck for the Pi rail.
Set output with a meter under load before connecting electronics; lock the pot with a dab of glue.

components.name: 3S LiPo 3000 mAh

key_specs.voltage: 11.1 V nominal, 12.6 V full, 9.9 V (3.3 V/cell) practical cutoff
key_specs.discharge: check C rating; 25C x 3 Ah = 75 A burst

gotchas: Add a main fuse and a switch; add a low-voltage alarm or firmware cutoff using an ADC voltage divider.

components.name: FTC-legal 12 V NiMH robot battery (e.g., REV-31-1302)
gotchas: Follow the current season's competition manual for legal batteries, switches and wiring.
